newsitem.title: UK: EMU condition of any deal with Labour - UK Liberal.
newsitem.headline: EMU condition of any deal with Labour - UK Liberal.

text.p: The Liberal Democrats would not prop up a minority Labour government unless it was committed to Britain joining a single European currency in the first wave, their foreign affairs spokesman said on Sunday.

Menzies Campbell said a referendum on Britain's electoral system in which ministers backed a change to proportional representation would also be a precondition for any post-general election "arrangement."

The Liberals, Britain's third largest party, are likely to be Labour leader Tony Blair's preferred partner in a coalition or another pact if he fails to win an overall majority in an election which must be held by next May.
Blair looks set to win a big parliamentary majority as most opinion polls put Labour some 20 points ahead of the ruling Conservatives.
Campbell, interviewed on independent television, said a so-called "hung" parliament was a statistically unlikely outcome to the election.
But he said if the Liberals held the balance of power, they could not give away two of their most precious policy stances in return for ministerial posts for a few of their leaders.

"How can you campaign in the country, make speeches as we do about the significance and importance of these two key parts of our policies and then suggest that in return for some kind of loose association...one would simply abandon these," he said.
"Europe is absolutely central to our political beliefs and philosophy...the people of the United Kingdom can look to us as being the rock in relation to Europe," he added.

The Liberal Democrats are pledged to the principle that Britain should hold a referendum if the government proposes changes, such as joining a single currency, which alter Britain's constitutional relationship with the European Union.
